Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- What the failing test asserts:
  - In DOMModelTest.testAxisAttribute(), the last check asserts that evaluating "vendor/product/price:amount/attribute::node()" returns the set {"10%", "20%"} (lines 561–566). This expression selects all attribute nodes on the price:amount element, so two attributes are expected.

- How attribute::node() is compiled:
  - The XPath parser builds a step with axis=attribute and a node test. For node(), the parser generates a node type test (Compiler.NODE_TYPE_NODE), not a name test. This comes from the parser’s NodeTest rule, which, when it matches a node type (like node()), calls compiler.nodeTypeTest(type).

- How attributes are iterated in the current implementation:
  - AttributeContext.nextNode() initializes the attribute iterator the first time it’s called (lines 73–81).
  - It currently has:
    - if (!(nodeTest instanceof NodeNameTest)) return false; (lines 75–77)
    - Otherwise, it extracts the QName from NodeNameTest and calls parentContext.getCurrentNodePointer().attributeIterator(name) (lines 78–81).

- Why attribute::node() fails:
  - For attribute::node(), nodeTest is not a NodeNameTest but a node type test (i.e., matches any node on the attribute axis). Because nextNode() rejects any nodeTest that is not a NodeNameTest, it immediately returns false, never initializing the iterator, and yields an empty result.
  - Hence, the assertion expecting {"10%", "20%"} fails because no attributes are returned.

- Evidence aligning with the user’s bug report:
  - The report points directly to AttributeContext line 72 and suggests handling a wildcard, proposing a WILDCARD QName = new QName("", "*"). This matches the required behavior: on the attribute axis, node() should match all attribute nodes, which can be implemented by iterating attributes with a wildcard name.
  - The suggested fix pattern is: if nodeTest is a NodeNameTest, use its name; else if nodeTest is a node type test for node(), treat it as a wildcard and pass WILDCARD to attributeIterator; otherwise, return false.

- Conclusion (root cause):
  - AttributeContext.nextNode() only supports NodeNameTest and incorrectly rejects node-type tests such as node() on the attribute axis. This prevents attribute::node() from returning any attributes. The method should interpret node() on the attribute axis as a wildcard selection of all attributes (e.g., by using a wildcard QName), instead of returning false.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
